subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
unit: Across Cultures · Reading for Pleasure · Review and Reference
lesson: Reading for Pleasure: The Ethics of Advertising / Review and Reference: Theme 1 learning objectives and core words test
outcomes: Read an article about ethics in advertising for gist and detail
Decide whether advertising techniques are ethical and give reasons
Review the Theme 1 core words and the past simple passive

tf.s: Campbell's put marbles in soup bowls to push the vegetables to the top.
tf.why: Correct, the soup looked full of vegetables.

tf.s: A TV advert usually lasts several minutes, so it can give all the information.
tf.why: A TV ad lasts no more than 30 seconds.

tf.s: 'Four out of five doctors recommend Brand X' was meaningless because people did not know how many doctors were asked.
tf.why: Right, the number of doctors consulted was unknown.

tf.s: After the court case, McDonald's stopped selling food completely.
tf.why: It added nutritional information and offered healthier food.

tf.s: A 'shopaholic' is someone who is addicted to shopping.
tf.why: Yes, like an alcoholic, but for shopping.

tf.s: 'Export' means selling goods to another country.
tf.why: Correct; import means buying from another country.

tf.s: 'Mislead' means to give people the right information.
tf.why: Mislead means to make people believe something wrong.

tf.s: The past simple passive of 'discover' (singular) is 'was discovered'.

boxes.q: Why did Campbell's put marbles in the soup?
o: to push the vegetables to the top
boxes.why: It made the soup look full of vegetables.

boxes.q: How long does a TV ad usually last?
What is a 'mock-up' in an advert?
o: a model that looks like the real product
a true photo of the product
boxes.why: Mock-ups, like shaving cream for ice-cream, are not the real thing.

boxes.q: What did McDonald's offer after the case?
boxes.why: It offered healthier options and nutritional information.
Excessive means more than is reasonable.

boxes.q: Which word means 'someone addicted to shopping'?

boxes.why: Import means buying from another country.

o: unwanted effects of something, such as a medicine
mcq.why: Side-effects are extra, often bad, results.

mcq.q: What did McDonald's do after the 2002 court case?
o: put nutritional information in restaurants and online and offered healthier food
mcq.why: It gave more information and healthier choices.

mcq.q: Why is it hard to give a lot of information in an advert?
o: TV ads are short and print space is limited

mcq.q: An ice-cream ad uses shaving cream because real ice-cream melts under the lights. What is this?
mcq.why: It is a model that is not the real product.

mcq.q: Complete: The mistake ___ (discover) by the teacher.
Choose the sentence that uses 'mislead' correctly.
o: Some adverts mislead customers about what a product can do.
I mislead my lunch at noon.
She misleads very fast in the race.
mcq.why: Mislead means give a wrong idea.

mcq.q: Why was the claim 'four out of five doctors recommend Brand X' meaningless?
o: the public couldn't know how many doctors were consulted
mcq.why: Without the total number, the claim proves nothing.

mcq.q: Why do many people think the Campbell's marbles were unethical?
o: the soup looked as if it had more vegetables than it really had
mcq.why: It gave buyers a false picture of the product.

mcq.q: How does 'caveat emptor' connect to misleading adverts?
o: buyers must be careful because ads may not tell the whole truth
mcq.why: Let the buyer beware means check claims carefully.
